subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Where Is Everybody?
description: Learn Where Is Everybody? in one minute.

hook.text: The galaxy is vast and old. If intelligent life is common, someone should have visited or contacted us by now. No one has.

buildup.text: Enrico Fermi posed this question over lunch in 1950. The contradiction between probability and silence is the Fermi Paradox.

discovery.text: The Milky Way is 13.6 billion years old. A civilization with modest technology could colonize the galaxy in a few million years.

twist.text: The paradox assumes life is common and technology inevitable. If either assumption is wrong, silence makes perfect sense.

climax.text: The paradox has dozens of proposed solutions. None is proven, and the silence remains one of science's most haunting puzzles.

punchline.text: Billions of years, billions of stars. Yet silence. That's the paradox.

quiz.question: What is the Fermi Paradox?
options: The contradiction between the high probability of alien life and the lack of evidence for it
The observation that the universe is expanding faster than light can travel
The mathematical proof that intelligent life can only arise once per galaxy

details.summary: Enrico Fermi's famous paradox asks: if the galaxy is old enough for civilizations to have colonized it many times over, why have we found no evidence of any? Given billions of years and hundreds of billions of stars, the apparent silence is deeply puzzling and demands explanation.
details.whyItMatters: The Fermi Paradox is the central problem of astrobiology and SETI. Every proposed solution — life is rare, civilizations self-destruct, they're hiding — carries profound implications for humanity's future.
takeaways: Fermi asked why no evidence of alien civilizations exists
The galaxy is old enough for colonization many times over
Every proposed solution has profound implications for humanity

faq.question: What are the main solutions to the Fermi Paradox?
faq.answer: They cluster into three categories: life or intelligence is extremely rare (Rare Earth); civilizations exist but are undetectable or uninterested in contact (zoo hypothesis, dark forest); or civilizations inevitably self-destruct before interstellar travel (Great Filter).

faq.question: When did Fermi pose his paradox?
faq.answer: During a 1950 lunch at Los Alamos, Fermi reportedly asked 'Where is everybody?' during a conversation about aliens and interstellar travel. The question became formalized as a paradox because reasonable assumptions about the number of civilizations predict we should see evidence.
